lines: Juna: Fresh off the ferry? I'm Juna. I carry letters between the regions.
Juna: Madderby is up the river road. Follow the colours, or what's left of them.
Juna: Guild apprentice now? Then you'll be getting post from me. Mind the moor.
Juna: Ashmere? I go there twice a week. Bring a scarf. The ash gets everywhere.
Ysolde: You have Mirela's compass rose on your map case. Where did you get that?
Ysolde: ...Her grandchild. Of course. You draw like her. Too fast.
Ysolde: I am Ysolde Rennick, master of this guild. Forty years ago I let Mirela walk into a Rift alone.
Ysolde: I won't make that mistake twice. From today you are an apprentice of the guild.
Ysolde: Two Rifts tear at Corvane: the Rain Rift in the Woadfen and the Mirror Rift at Stillwater. Mend them, and the colours come back.
Ysolde: The Rain Rift lies in the Woadfen, the Mirror Rift past Stillwater. Either order.
Ysolde: Both Rifts mended. Look at the river. Red again, and blue, and gold.
Ysolde: You've seen the Wide Rift. Sit down, apprentice. There is something in the guild files.
Ysolde: The railway to Ashmere leaves from the north end of town. Halvard will be expecting you.
Pim: Pim, archivist. Well, the only archivist. Ask me anything about Rifts. Please. Nobody ever asks.
Pim: What do you want to know?

pim_hush: Pim: Veydal calls it the Hush. Here we say the Fading, because it drains colour, not just voices.
Pim: In Ashmere they say the Stilling. Spirlings there freeze where they stand.

lines: Pim: Mirela wrote to Aldo for years before she left. Some letters never reached him.
Pim: Three are somewhere in Corvane, three more in Ashmere. Bring me any you find.
Pim: All three Corvane letters! 'I'll paint the lighthouse door blue.' Did she ever?
Pim: Take these, for the road. Three more letters wait in Ashmere, I'm sure of it.
Pim: All six! 'Tell them to sing. Not fight.' I'm copying these into the guild records.
Pim: Here. Ysolde said you've earned the good tonic.
THE GUILD WALL MAP
Corvane is drawn in grey. Only the river is coloured, in faded blue.
THE GUILD WALL MAP
The Woadfen glows blue again. The rest of Corvane is still grey.
THE GUILD WALL MAP
Stillwater shines silver. The rest of Corvane is still grey.
THE GUILD WALL MAP
All of Corvane is coloured in. Only the Wide Rift in the north is left blank.
An old desk with V. HARROW cut into the edge. In the drawer: a collar tag that says ASH.
A shelf of burned maps. One survived: Greyreach, with a small Mirkmole drawn in the margin.
Ash in the stove, and a note half burned: '...twenty years and still no answer when I call...'
Ash was a Mirkmole. Veit's Mirkmole. Whatever Veit is now, he started out grieving.
Dyer: My vats used to run red as a sunset. Now? Grey, grey, grey.
Dyer: Bring me a Riptail with its colour back and I'll believe the Fading can end.
Dyer: Look at that red! I'm dyeing a whole bolt in its honour.
Dyer: Gold comes from Glimmerax scales, shed in spring. None shed this year.
Dyer: If you have a Glimmerax that still shines, show me.
Dyer: Gold again. My grandmother would cry.
Dyer: Green is the hardest colour. It takes a Mossling's patience.
Dyer: Show me a Mossling with real green on it and I'll teach you the old word for hope.
Dyer: The old word for hope is 'verd'. Now you know.
The three dye families wave cloth in red, gold and green from their windows.
Kestra: There you are. I'm mapping the colour layers in the river. Look, the grey runs downstream from the Woadfen.
Kestra: Tatter unfurled on the way here. A Tempestrel now. Still a frayed wing, see?
Kestra: I'm not saying you're right. I'm saying I need to check the guild files myself.
Tatter shivers on Kestra's arm, silent.
You hum the Echo melody, low, the way Aldo hums at the lamp.
Tatter's frayed wing twitches. Then, very quietly, it chirps.
Kestra: ...It answered you. It hasn't answered anyone since the Woadfen.

kestra_sing_fail: Tatter stays quiet, but it leans toward you a little.
kestra_space: You step back and let Kestra hold Tatter close.
Kestra: ...Thanks. I just need a minute.
kestra_2_intro: Kestra: Every Rift you mend, Spirlings like Tatter get sicker. That's what I see.
Kestra: So show me. Show me your way works. Battle me!

lines: Kestra: ...Fine. You fight like someone who believes it.
Kestra: Tell me honestly. Does what I think even matter to you?

kestra_2_matters: Kestra: ...Okay. Then let's find out the truth. Together, for once.
kestra_2_mend: Kestra: I know. That's what scares me.

lines: Senna: ...rain. Only rain. Can you hear it? It never stops.
Senna: The rain stopped. I can hear the moor birds again. And my Riptail. Thank you.
Senna: Rain is just weather again. I'd forgotten it could smell this good.
Senna: Some days it still rains. But now it's only weather.

senna_intro: Senna: ...rain. Only rain. Can you hear it?
Senna: If you want to pass, you'll have to wake me. Riptail! ...Riptail?
senna_defeat: Senna: ...Oh. I can hear you. I can hear my Spirlings again.
Senna: Quickly, while my bond holds. Help me draw the edge of this Rift.

lines: Joral: In the Rift I only see myself. Everywhere. Always me.
Joral: Once, in the mirror, I saw an old woman with a compass. She smiled at me.
Joral: I thought I'd imagined her. Now I'm not so sure.
Joral: I look into the pond now and see the sky. Strange, how good that feels.

joral_intro: Joral: Another reflection? No... you're real. That's worse.
Joral: Show me something that isn't me!
joral_defeat: Joral: My Lumenewt... it's looking at me, not at itself. It sees me.
Joral: Help me close this. Before I forget the way out again.
veit_intro: Veit: A guild apprentice. They still send children to fix the Rifts.
Veit: You can't mend a wound that keeps opening. You burn it out. Let me show you.

lines: Veit: Strong bond. Mirela's blood, I suppose.
Veit: The Wide Rift took more than her. It took my Ash. I'll see it erased.

veit_leaves: Veit gathers his maps and heads north, toward the Ashmere railway.

lines: Moss: Mirela? I knew her. We charted the Greyreach together, fifty years ago.
Moss: She walked into that light up north and never came out. She's gone, child.
Moss: She's alive? Ha! I owe Ysolde a bottle. Fifty years of being wrong. Worth it.
Words are burned into the rock at the very edge of the Rift, in a hand you know.
'Still drawing. Still here. M.'

kestra_2_lose: Kestra: See? Maybe I'm not as wrong as you think.
Kestra: Rest up. I'll be here by the river.

lines: Ysolde: She's alive. Mirela is alive, and you found her. Give me a moment, apprentice.
Ysolde: ...There. The guild names you cartographer. Not apprentice. Never again.
Kestra: Shh. Look at the terraces. Two Wanderers, walking in circles.
Kestra: The Hush has them. Their Spirlings won't even look up.
Kestra: I can't wake them alone. Tatter's too tired. ...Fight with me?
The two Wanderers blink, as if waking from a long walk.
Kestra: We did that. Both of us, side by side.
Kestra: ...Maybe your way and mine aren't so far apart.

kestra_tag_lose: Kestra: Too much Hush for one day. Rest up. I'll keep watch on them.
kestra_still_after: Kestra: The Wanderers went home. Tatter keeps looking at the pond. I think it's smiling.

lines: Wanderer Hale: I walked into the fen to find my Spirling. Then I forgot why I was walking.
Wanderer Hale: Days, maybe weeks. The rain sang the same note over and over.
Wanderer Hale: When the Rift closed, my Riptail licked my hand. That's how I knew I was awake.
Wanderer Brisa: I was a dyer in Madderby. I came out here to gather woad, and the Hush came with the rain.
Wanderer Brisa: I still can't remember the colour of my own front door. Blue, I think. I'll go and see.
Juna: Post for you! From the lighthouse.
"{name}, the lake was calm this morning, and I thought of you. The Kelpups miss your boots. Eat something warm. Aldo."
Juna: Another one from Brindlewick. He writes small.
"Kestra's mother came by asking after her. I said you two keep an eye on each other. Don't make me a liar. Aldo."
Juna: Last one before Ashmere. This one's heavy. I think it's mostly worry.
"Mirela wrote me once from Ashmere. She said the ash tastes like old pencils. If you see her... tell her the lamp is lit. Aldo."
Weda: The dye spring runs warm and red. Spirlings come out of it brighter than they went in.
Weda: Sit. Let the colour do the work.
An abandoned cartographer's hut. On the table lies a diary, its edges singed.
"Day one. Ash walked into the Wide Rift after a moth. I called until my voice gave out."
"Day forty. The guild says wait, map it, mend it. I mapped it. It took him anyway."
"Last page. If a map can open a Rift, a fire can close one. I will burn them all. V. H."
